studies.Reference: Levels of zinc, selenium, calcium, and iron in benign breast tissue and risk of subsequent breast cancer.
studies.Authors: Cui Y, Vogt S, Olson N, Glass AG, Rohan TE
studies.Journal: Cancer epidemiology, biomarkers & prevention : a publication of the American Association for Cancer Research, cosponsored by the American Society of Preventive Oncology
studies.exposure_measurement_supporting_text: Elemental levels in breast tissue were directly measured using X-ray fluorescence spectroscopy.

extraction_supporting_text.sample_size: A cohort of 9,315 women with benign breast disease.
extraction_supporting_text.effect_size: Quintile analyses revealed positive associations of breast cancer, of borderline statistical significance, with zinc [highest versus lowest quintile: odds ratio (OR), 1.37].
extraction_supporting_text.effect_direction: Positive associations of breast cancer with zinc.
extraction_supporting_text.outcome_definition: We investigated these associations by directly measuring elemental levels in breast tissue.
extraction_supporting_text.exposure_definition: Elemental levels in breast tissue were directly measured using X-ray fluorescence spectroscopy.

studies.Reference: Serum zinc and dietary intake of zinc in relation to risk of different breast cancer subgroups and serum levels as a marker of intake: a prospective nested case-control study.
studies.Authors: Bengtsson Y, Sandsveden M, Borgquist S, Manjer J
studies.exposure_measurement_supporting_text: Serum zinc was measured as a marker of dietary intake.

extraction_supporting_text.sample_size: 1186 incident cases were identified and matched to an equal number of controls.
extraction_supporting_text.effect_size: The adjusted OR for breast cancer in serum zinc Q4 compared to Q1 was 1.09 (0.85-1.41).
extraction_supporting_text.effect_direction: No associations were found between zinc, measured in serum or diet pre-diagnostically, and breast cancer risk.
extraction_supporting_text.outcome_definition: Breast cancer risk was assessed in relation to serum zinc levels.
extraction_supporting_text.exposure_definition: Serum zinc was measured as a marker of dietary intake.

studies.Reference: Zinc and copper in breast cancer. A joint study in northern Italy and southern France.
studies.Authors: Cavallo F, Gerber M, Marubini E, Richardson S, Barbieri A, Costa A, DeCarli A, Pujol H
studies.exposure_measurement_supporting_text: Blood levels of Zn and Cu were measured in 261 cases and 261 controls.

extraction_supporting_text.effect_size: The pooled OR computed from the two samples, after adjustment for known risk factors and related variables, reaches in the fourth quartile a value of 9.5.
extraction_supporting_text.effect_direction: Zn mean values are significantly higher in cases than in controls.
extraction_supporting_text.p_value: No odds ratios (OR) in the different quantiles, nor X2 for trend reached statistical significance.
extraction_supporting_text.outcome_definition: The relationship between breast cancer and two trace elements, zinc (Zn) and copper (Cu), was investigated.
extraction_supporting_text.exposure_definition: Blood levels of Zn and Cu were measured in 261 cases and 261 controls.

studies.Reference: Association of Dietary Intake of Zinc and Selenium with Breast Cancer Risk: A Case-Control Study in Chinese Women.
studies.Authors: Tu K, Liu K, Wang Y, Jiang Y, Zhang C
studies.exposure_measurement_supporting_text: Dietary intake was collected using a validated food frequency questionnaire.

extraction_supporting_text.sample_size: The case-control study included 1591 cases and 1622 age-frequency matched controls.
extraction_supporting_text.effect_size: Zn from white meat intake was linearly and inversely associated with breast cancer risk, with adjusted odds ratio and 95% confidence interval of 0.76 (0.61-0.95).
extraction_supporting_text.effect_direction: Zn from white meat intake was linearly and inversely associated with breast cancer risk.
extraction_supporting_text.outcome_definition: This study aimed to investigate the relationship between dietary Zn, Se intake and breast cancer risk in Chinese women.
extraction_supporting_text.exposure_definition: Dietary Zn and Se were divided into four categories: Zn/Se from plants, Zn/Se from meat, Zn/Se from red meat, and Zn/Se from white meat.

studies.Reference: Toenail trace element levels and breast cancer: a prospective study.
studies.Authors: Garland M, Morris JS, Colditz GA, Stampfer MJ, Spate VL, Baskett CK, Rosner B, Speizer FE, Willett WC, Hunter DJ
studies.exposure_measurement_supporting_text: Toenail levels of trace elements were measured.

extraction_supporting_text.sample_size: 62,641 US women who provided toenail clippings and were free from diagnosed breast cancer in 1982.
extraction_supporting_text.effect_direction: These results do not provide evidence for an important effect of arsenic, copper, chromium, iron, or zinc on breast cancer risk.
extraction_supporting_text.outcome_definition: 433 cases of breast cancer identified during 4 years of follow-up.
extraction_supporting_text.exposure_definition: Toenail levels of five trace elements.

studies.Reference: Dietary Antioxidant Vitamins and Minerals and Breast Cancer Risk: Prospective Results from the SUN Cohort.
studies.Authors: Fernandez-Lazaro CI, Martínez-González MÁ, Aguilera-Buenosvinos I, Gea A, Ruiz-Canela M, Romanos-Nanclares A, Toledo E
studies.exposure_measurement_supporting_text: Participants completed a food frequency questionnaire at baseline.

extraction_supporting_text.sample_size: 9983 female participants from the SUN Project.
extraction_supporting_text.effect_direction: Our results did not suggest significant protective associations between dietary vitamins A, C, and E, selenium, or zinc and BC risk.
extraction_supporting_text.outcome_definition: Biennial follow-up information about incident BC diagnosis was collected.
extraction_supporting_text.exposure_definition: Dietary intake of vitamins A, C, and E, selenium, and zinc.

studies.Reference: The role of diet history and biologic assays in the study of "diet and breast cancer".
studies.Authors: Gerber M, Richardson S, Cavallo F, Marubini E, Crastes de Paulet P, Crastes de Paulet A, Pujol H
studies.exposure_measurement_supporting_text: Serum zinc was assessed in the Italian samples.

extraction_supporting_text.effect_direction: zinc serum level was higher in Italian cases than in Italian controls.
extraction_supporting_text.outcome_definition: Nutritional factors related to breast cancer were investigated.
extraction_supporting_text.exposure_definition: Serum zinc was assessed in the Italian samples.

studies.Reference: Raw and cooked vegetables, fruits, selected micronutrients, and breast cancer risk: a case-control study in Germany.
studies.Authors: Adzersen KH, Jess P, Freivogel KW, Gerhard I, Bastert G
studies.exposure_measurement_supporting_text: High intake of some selected vitamins and minerals possessing putative DNA-stabilizing properties displayed significant inverse risk associations.

extraction_supporting_text.sample_size: Three hundred ten consecutively recruited cases with primary breast cancer were matched according to 10-yr age groups to 353 controls.
extraction_supporting_text.effect_size: Adjusted ORs were as follows: zinc (OR = 0.35, 95% CI = 0.15-0.78).
extraction_supporting_text.effect_direction: High intake of zinc displayed significant inverse risk associations.
extraction_supporting_text.outcome_definition: A case-control study of breast cancer was conducted in Heidelberg, Germany.
extraction_supporting_text.exposure_definition: High intake of some selected vitamins and minerals possessing putative DNA-stabilizing properties.

studies.Reference: Antioxidants and breast cancer risk- a population-based case-control study in Canada.
studies.Authors: Pan SY, Zhou J, Gibbons L, Morrison H, Wen SW,
studies.exposure_measurement_supporting_text: Intakes of antioxidants from diet and from supplementation as well as other potential risk factors for breast cancer were collected by a self-reported questionnaire.

extraction_supporting_text.sample_size: The study population included 2,362 cases with pathologically confirmed incident breast cancer (866 premenopausal and 1,496 postmenopausal) and 2,462 controls in Canada.
extraction_supporting_text.effect_size: 10 years or longer supplementation of zinc had multivariable-adjusted odds ratios (OR) and 95% confidence intervals (CI) of 0.46 (0.25-0.85) for premenopausal women.
extraction_supporting_text.effect_direction: 10 years or longer supplementation of zinc had multivariable-adjusted odds ratios (OR) and 95% confidence intervals (CI) of 0.46 (0.25-0.85) for premenopausal women.
extraction_supporting_text.outcome_definition: The study population included 2,362 cases with pathologically confirmed incident breast cancer.
extraction_supporting_text.exposure_definition: 10 years or longer supplementation of zinc.

studies.Reference: Serum Essential Elements and Survival after Cancer Diagnosis.
studies.Authors: Lubiński J, Lener MR, Marciniak W, Pietrzak S, Derkacz R, Cybulski C, Gronwald J, Dębniak T, Jakubowska A, Huzarski T, Matuszczak M, Pullella K, Sun P, Narod SA

headline.funnel_interpretation: Egger's test indicates no significant funnel plot asymmetry (p=0.7514). The distribution of studies appears symmetric, suggesting a lower risk of publication bias.
headline.results_interpretation: The pooled analysis of 10 studies yielded an effect size of 1.14 (95% CI: 0.68–1.91), indicating no statistically significant association between zinc and uterine cancer. Although the point estimate suggests a potential positive relationship, the confidence interval includes the null. These findings were accompanied by very high heterogeneity (I² = 96.25%), reflecting highly inconsistent results across studies.
